channel.title: Proxly Updates
channel.description: Updates for Proxly - Smart Browser Chooser

item.title: Version 1.7.1
item.description:
Added

  • Chrome, Brave, Comet, Edge and Firefox: links can stay in the current tab: with the Proxly extension’s new “Keep links in this tab” option, a link Proxly would open in the same browser anyway now opens in the current tab instead of a new one (proxly-releases#5)
    • Set it up in Settings → Browser Extensions, or with “Set up in Proxly” in the extension’s popup
    • Links Proxly would send elsewhere (another browser, a profile, a private window, a transformation, the browser chooser) still go to Proxly, as do ⌘-clicks and links that open a new window
    • The App Store version needs the latest ProxlyHelper; Settings says when it needs updating
    • Needs version 1.1 of the Proxly extension, which follows shortly

Fixed

  • Safari extension: links to other sites no longer reopen in a new tab: with “Capture all external links” on, every link that left the page’s site went to Proxly, and when Proxly’s answer was Safari itself the link came back as a new tab
    • Links Proxly would open in Safari unchanged — no matching rule with Safari as your fallback browser, or a rule that targets plain Safari — now open in the current tab, without the “→ Proxly” flash
    • Links left in the current tab never reach Proxly, so they are not added to History and do not trigger the fallback notification
    • Moving between subdomains of the same site (docs.example.com → www.example.com), or from http to https, no longer counts as leaving the site
    • Links that need Proxly — another browser, a profile, a private window, a transformation, the browser chooser, or a short link Proxly expands first — go to Proxly exactly as before, as do ⌘-clicks, links that open in a new window, and “Open with Proxly”
    • Same-tab navigation is Safari-only for now; the Chrome and Firefox extensions still hand these links to Proxly
  • No more “Data Access Blocked” notifications on macOS 27: macOS 27 stops apps from reading Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox data unless you allowed it, and shows a notification whenever Proxly checked your browser profiles in the background — including at every login
    • Proxly now remembers your browser profiles between launches and reads them only right after you grant access, when you press Refresh, or when you open a profile picker (at most once an hour) — no longer at every login or in the background
    • If macOS blocks access, Proxly shows “Blocked by macOS” with buttons to choose the folder again or open Privacy & Security, instead of silently showing no profiles
    • A blocked read no longer erases your profile list or removes profiles from your browser order
    • The Grant Access panel now checks that you picked the browser’s own data folder
  • Applications in subfolders are now discovered: Proxly listed the standard application directories only one level deep, so anything kept in a subfolder — for example /Applications/AdditionalApplications or /Applications/Utilities — was invisible and could not be picked as a browser or used in rules
    • The standard locations are now scanned recursively, so vendor layouts such as /Applications/Adobe/Acrobat/ are covered
    • Browsers and mail apps the system already knows about are additionally discovered through LaunchServices, so they are found wherever they are installed — including outside the standard locations entirely
    • Safari is now found through the same general mechanism rather than a dedicated workaround
    • When several copies of the same application are installed, Proxly lists the one macOS would actually launch, so the entry you pick matches what opens
